business_problem: Utah needed to migrate its eligibility software to a compliant cloud platform without giving up MongoDB, while still supporting large electronic case files, fast caseworker response times, and strong disaster recovery for public-benefits workflows.
solution_summary: The State of Utah runs its eREP eligibility application on MongoDB Atlas for Government (US), a FedRAMP Moderate-authorized managed service chosen to meet security requirements without sacrificing performance. eREP stores electronic case files as BSON documents and uses a rules engine to determine benefits across more than 60 social services, which makes fast document storage and retrieval critical. To meet its migration deadline before Atlas for Government completed FedRAMP approval, the department first moved the workload to self-managed Amazon EC2 and then, four months later, migrated again into the managed MongoDB Atlas for Government environment. In the final architecture, case data stays in MongoDB, the eligibility engine reads those documents directly, and Atlas handles alerts, backup, scaling, and point-in-time restore. That fully managed design gives caseworkers faster access to results while removing manual shard, failover, and scripting work from the technology team.

business_outcome: MongoDB Atlas for Government made eREP 25% faster than the on-premises system, shortened disaster-recovery time from up to 58 hours to less than five minutes, and reduced operational effort for the state's database team.
